statements.status_notes: CVE-2016-2781: chroot in GNU coreutils, run with --userspec, leaves the program it starts attached to the caller's terminal, so that program can push characters into the parent session's input with the TIOCSTI ioctl and have the parent shell run them (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2016-2781, Debian bug https://bugs.debian.org/816320). GNU coreutils has not changed chroot for this. The mitigation is in the Linux kernel: since Linux 6.2, TIOCSTI can be switched off with the CONFIG_LEGACY_TIOCSTI build option or the dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti sysctl (https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=83efeeeb3d04b22aaed1df99bc70a48fe9d22c4d), and since Linux 6.5 processes with CAP_SYS_ADMIN can still use it when it is switched off (https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=690c8b804ad2eafbd35da5d3c95ad325ca7d5061). Debian builds its kernels with CONFIG_LEGACY_TIOCSTI unset (Debian bug https://bugs.debian.org/1033095), and its security tracker marks the CVE fixed from coreutils 9.4-1 on that basis rather than for a coreutils change. Alpine lists coreutils 9.8-r1 for 3.23 as not fixed (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2016-2781). In a container, whether TIOCSTI is available depends on the host kernel and its settings, not on this package, so no property of the published coreutils builds (9.8-r1 and 9.8-r2) settles it. Pending a maintainer decision on whether a host-kernel mitigation is enough to record this owner as not affected, it stays under investigation.
